I'll start by reading the script and checking what the profiler can measure.
Profiling the script with the V8 CPU profiler now.
The profiler's output write was blocked by the sandbox (EPERM). I'll run Node's built-in profiler directly into a scratch directory outside the repo, then read the result.
`isPrime` in `scripts/slow.mjs:2` is the slowest function, taking about 1.78s of the roughly 2.3s run (77% self time). It's called from `countPrimes` for every n up to 60,000, and its trial-division loop runs up to n iterations for each number.

`dedupe` (line 12) is a distant second at about 215ms (9%), since `out.includes` scans the output array on each step. The rest is Node startup and module loading.

The profiler's built-in `cpu` op failed with an EPERM write error in the sandbox, so I ran `node --cpu-prof` directly and analyzed the saved profile in Volt. The profile is in `/tmp/slowprof`, outside the repo, and I didn't change any files.
